long_biography.plain_text:
Born in Amman and educated in Jordan, Britain and the United States, Abdullah attended the Royal Military Academy Sandhurst before building a career in Jordan's armed forces. He rose to major general and commanded the country's special forces, combining military responsibility with periods as regent for his father, King Hussein.

He assumed the throne in 1999 and has centred much of his public work on regional security, dialogue and religious coexistence. The Amman Message set out an Islamic case against extremism, while his proposal for World Interfaith Harmony Week was adopted unanimously by the United Nations. The annual observance now brings governments, institutions and civil society together each February around programmes intended to strengthen understanding across faiths.
